$comment: Provenance manifest for UrbanPulse. This file is the only place where a
dataset may be introduced to the platform: scripts/register_data_sources.py
loads it into the `data_sources` table, and every stored observation
carries a foreign key to one of these rows.
Licence and URL fields were transcribed from each provider's published
documentation on the date below. Re-verify them before running an
ingestion job — terms change, and attribution obligations are ours to meet.
`origin` is the honesty flag: `observed` is measured by an external
authority, `derived` is computed by UrbanPulse from observed inputs, and
`simulated` is produced by the simulation layer and is never real-world
truth. The API and the UI surface this value directly.

datasets.name: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5 reanalysis)
datasets.attribution: Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (ERA5 reanalysis, Copernicus Climate Change Service)
datasets.description: Hourly historical precipitation, temperature, humidity, wind and soil moisture on a reanalysis grid. Supplies the antecedent-rainfall features and the training window. No API key required.
datasets.role: Primary training input for rainfall features.

datasets.name: Open-Meteo Forecast API
datasets.description: Hourly precipitation forecast used at inference time. Rows are stored with is_forecast = true so forecasts are never mixed with measurements when training.

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap road network (via Overpass API)
datasets.description: Road centrelines with highway class, lane count, bridge and tunnel tags. Becomes the NetworkX graph used to find severed links during impact analysis.

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap administrative boundaries (via Overpass API)
datasets.description: Ward polygons used as the unit of analysis. Chosen over a municipal shapefile because coverage is consistent across cities, which keeps the platform portable beyond the first target city.

datasets.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (30 m global digital elevation model)
datasets.license: Copernicus DEM open licence (free use with attribution)
datasets.attribution: © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
datasets.description: Elevation raster from which mean and minimum elevation, slope and topographic depressions are derived per zone. Low-lying, flat zones are the strongest structural predictor of waterlogging.

known_gaps.need: Historical waterlogging incident records for the target city
known_gaps.why_it_matters: These are the supervised labels. Without them the risk model cannot be trained or evaluated, and no probability can honestly be reported.
known_gaps.status: No authoritative open dataset identified. Municipal complaint logs are not published as open data for Mumbai.
candidate_approaches: Request the MCGM disaster-management complaint log through a formal data request.
Derive weak labels from geotagged news and social reports, stored with origin = 'derived' and a documented extraction method.
Use a published academic flood-inundation dataset for the city if licensing permits.

known_gaps.need: Storm-water drainage network and pumping-station capacity
known_gaps.why_it_matters: Drainage capacity determines how much rainfall a zone absorbs before surface water accumulates; without it the model must infer capacity indirectly from terrain and imperviousness.
known_gaps.status: Not published as open data. The drainage_assets table stays empty until a real dataset is registered.
candidate_approaches: OpenStreetMap waterway=drain / nallah geometry as a partial proxy, clearly marked as incomplete.

known_gaps.why_it_matters: High tide blocks gravity drainage in coastal cities; rainfall coinciding with high tide is the classic severe-waterlogging pattern.
known_gaps.status: Source not yet confirmed. INCOIS publishes tide predictions for Indian ports but the access terms need checking before use.
candidate_approaches: Confirm INCOIS tide prediction access terms.
Evaluate a commercial tide API if open access is unavailable.

known_gaps.why_it_matters: Would let impact analysis be validated against observed congestion instead of inferred from road-graph connectivity alone.
known_gaps.status: No open real-time feed for the target city. Impact analysis will therefore report structural road impact, not measured congestion, and must say so.
candidate_approaches: Commercial traffic API if the project acquires a key.
